worcester-R8613.summary: Girolamo Ghinucci, Bishop of Worcester, at the Emperor's court, reports that the Imperialists want to draw Henry VIII to themselves and part him from the French king, that the French offered three millions through Avemaria, that the Imperial envoy to the Pope has no commission for his release, and the rumour that Wolsey goes to France to separate the English and French church from Rome 'ad perpetuam divisionem'. L&P iv 3291 records that this duplicate was not deciphered at the time; 17 of 814 tokens remain open.
worcester-R8613.en:
⟨The Imperialists⟩ seem above all ⟨to wish to have […], ho[…]⟩ to take care and in some way to hope that by some
means ⟨they may draw the King's Majesty to themselves⟩, so that at least ⟨they may separate him from the King of the
French; and as long as⟩ he has persuaded himself that he can hope for this, ⟨I believe they⟩ think of nothing ⟨less⟩
than ⟨of peace⟩. And if he offered ⟨them richer conditions⟩, although for a certain show of honesty ⟨they say in words
that they want nothing else⟩. I well believe that, if ⟨this hope did not feed them, richer conditions having been
offered them […]⟩, it could be hoped well enough ⟨that […] they would come to [?peace]⟩. And much more could be
hoped, in my judgement, if ⟨they did not hold it for certain that the friendship and union between the King's Majesty
[and] the King of the French will not last long⟩.

worcester-R8589.summary: Sibling letter whose cipher passage is printed deciphered in L&P iv 5282 ('Cum animadvertissemus ...'); the file gives each token with its value aligned to that plaintext, and was the first key source.

worcester-R8476.summary: Sibling letter printed with its deciphered passages in State Papers Henry VIII vol. VI pp. 552-556 (from the contemporary Record Office decipher); the file aligns the 845 cipher tokens with that text and gave the code words (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Cesar, Pontifex ...).

snip.cap: Cotton Vesp. C IV f. 363r: “Dupplicata sub die xxii Julii 1527” and the first line of Ghinucci’s cipher
snip.credit: British Library, Cotton MS Vespasian C IV f. 363r, via DECODE R8613

system: Syllabic substitution: base glyph = consonant row, superscript digit = syllable in the row (homophones), bare glyphs = single letters, a small code (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Cesar, Pontifex, Italia ...) and many nulls.
